subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost/pricing & latency trade-offs (FintechAI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps – cost vs latency trade-offs

Alex / Priya – thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key points from call:
- FintechAI is prototyping an in-product chat assistant for customer support and fraud triage.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~20M–30M tokens/month (peaks during batch jobs and marketing campaigns).
- Latency SLO: 95th %ile < 600ms for the chat path; 99th %ile target for critical flows if possible.
- Budget guidance: preliminary $3k–3k/mo while validating. Target unit economics: ideally $/1M tokens in the $100–250 range.

Trade-off considerations (high-level):
- Hosted standard tier gives fastest path: minimal ops, pay-as-you-go token pricing. Good for initial validation but higher $/1M.
- Dedicated/reserved gives better unit economics and stable p99 latency under heavy load, but requires commit (monthly/annual).
- Batching and KV-prefix caching can lower token cost ~25–50% depending on workload; large batches increase tail latency.
- Streaming (token-streamed responses) improves user-perceived latency but can increase cost surface for some models if you lose batching efficiency.
- SLO-driven pricing: we can map a premium SLA to reserved capacity + higher per-month fee; alternatives: route critical traffic to reserved pool and lower-priority traffic to hosted.

Proposed next steps:
1) You to confirm approximate token mix (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) and peak RPS patterns – helps us recommend tier and batching confidence.
2) We'll send a short pricing matrix + example unit economics for hosted vs dedicated at 20M/50M/100M tokens/month (attached).
3) If you can share a representative sample traffic pattern (anonymized), Rafael and Vivek can run a quick cost/latency simulation and propose configuration (batch settings, streaming on/off, model variants).
4) Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to go through numbers and trade-offs.

Attachments: 2026-07-01-fintechai-postcall-recap.pdf (slide recap)

Thanks \u2014
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps – cost vs latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa – helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side so your simulations can be more accurate:

- Token mix (best guess): chat generation ~70%, embeddings for search ~20%, reranking/other ~10%.
- Expected baseline: ~30M tokens/month for Q3 proof-of-concept. If POC succeeds, we expect it to grow to 60–80M within 6 months.
- Peak behavior: conversational traffic averages ~3–6 RPS with short bursts up to ~12 RPS for a few minutes post-email blasts.
- Latency tolerance: for agents embedded in the UI we want p95 < 400ms if possible; p99 under 800ms acceptable for now.
- Budget: the team is comfortable with $/1M tokens up to $200 during POC if latency targets are met.

Also – we've run into procurement timelines for enterprise vendors; if Redwood offers a short-term reserved window or pilot credits that could help speed decisioning.

Happy to share a small anonymized traffic dump (we'll remove any PII) – Priya will send that by EOD Friday.

Alex
Head of Product, FintechAI
alex.johnson@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps – cost vs latency trade-offs

Perfect – thanks for the details, Alex. That's exactly the level of signal we need. A few quick notes on mapping those numbers to options:

1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go) – good for POC when you want no commit and fast setup. Typical hosted unit price (example): $200/1M tokens for low-latency chat variants. At 30M tokens/mo this implies ~$6k/mo. With aggressive batching + prefix caching we often see effective unit cost drop to ~120–150/1M for conversational workloads.

2) Dedicated (reserved) – if you expect steady 50–80M tokens/mo and care about p99 tail, a reserved pool with a 3–6 month commit can get you to ~$100–140/1M effective. There are two levers: per-month reserved capacity fee (for guaranteed throughput and lower p99) plus a lower per-token price.

3) Batching + cache strategy – Rafael can run sims, but expected impact: 30%\u201345% cost reduction on generation token cost at the expense of slightly higher p99 unless we split critical flows to a low-latency pool.

4) Streaming vs batch – streaming is recommended for perceived latency (tokens appear sooner). If you need p95 < 400ms we typically keep small streaming window + micro-batching (batch windows < 50ms) to balance throughput. This can preserve near-interactive UX while still allowing some batching efficiency.

5) SLO-driven hybrid – route critical UI calls to a small reserved low-latency pool (higher $/1M but predictable p99) and route background or lower-priority calls to hosted with batching. That usually meets product constraints and reduces overall spend.

Next steps from Redwood: Rafael and Vivek will run a quick cost/latency simulation on the anonymized traffic you share. We'll return a short recommendation doc (hosted vs dedicated, suggested batch settings, streaming on/off, estimated $/1M after batching) + a sample pricing comparison for 30M/60M/80M tokens. We'll also include an optional pilot/reserved pricing we can offer for a 3-month pilot.

I'll pencil in a 30m slot next Wednesday. Rafael – can you take point on the sim? Vivek – can you draft the suggested batch/stream settings?

Thanks –
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps – cost vs latency trade-offs

Alex / team – attaching the initial pricing matrix and a short simulation summary based on the expected token mix and RPS profiles you described. High-level callouts:

- At 30M tokens/mo (70% chat mix) – hosted baseline estimate: $5.8k/mo (~$195/1M). With batching/cache settings (micro-batching + prefix caching) effective cost drops to ~$125/1M (~$3.75k/mo).
- At 60M tokens/mo – hosted baseline ~$11.7k/mo; dedicated reserved (3mo commit) estimate ~$6.8k–6.8k–140/1M) depending on reserved capacity size.
- For p95 < 400ms: micro-batching (batch window 20–50ms) + streaming enabled gives best perceived latency with ~10–20% higher compute compared to maximum-batched runs. We model this as a small uplift to cost.
- Recommendation: Pilot hybrid approach – small reserved low-latency pool sized for p95-critical traffic (estimate 20–30% of peak RPS) + hosted batched for the rest. This meets your p95 target while keeping effective blended $/1M in the $120–160 range during POC.

I've attached: redwood-pricing-matrix-2026.xlsx (pricing by token and reserved tiers), SOC2-summary.pdf, and a 1-page sim. Priya – once we get your anonymized traffic we can replace estimates with concrete sims.

Next actionable: Priya to upload anonymized traffic to the shared Drive link and we'll turn around a refined sim within 48 business hours. If you'd like, we can also prepare a short pilot contract (3-month reserved window with break clauses) to accelerate procurement.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix-2026.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf

Regards,
